title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten sheet bound among unrelated typescript (the neighbouring pages are an English paper on centralisers in reductive groups and a translated text on linear systems). It belongs to Grothendieck's 1965 'Galois theory of motives': motives over a finite field F_q, with q a power of p, and their motivic Galois group G(q), described through Weil numbers.

1. The fields. The margin diagram shows a tower Q ⊂ K ⊂ L. The caption has Q' next to K and Q'(i) next to L, so L is presumably a CM field (K(i)-type) and K a subfield. Subfields L_0 and K_0 are attached to a prime, and L/Q is assumed Galois ('galoisienne').

2. The Weil numbers. Let M(q) be the set of λ in L such that λλ̄ = q^i for some i (λ is a q-Weil number of weight i) and λ is an integer away from p. Let M_0 be the weight-0 part: λλ̄ = 1 and λ a unit away from p. The marginal N.B. notes that M_0 does not depend on q, M_0(q) = M_0(p), up to roots of unity.

3. The valuation map (*). Let P be the set of primes of L above p. Taking valuations at the primes ℘ in P gives a map M_0/torsion → (Z^P)'. By Kronecker's theorem the torsion (roots of unity) is exactly the kernel. The target (Z^P)' is the subgroup of functions with v_℘̄ = −v_℘, since λλ̄ = 1. So the character group of the Weil-number torus is described by p-adic valuations.

4. The cocharacter. He may assume the primes of K split (decompose) in L. He then fixes one prime ℘ above p and uses the valuation v_℘(λ). This gives a homomorphism v_L: G_{m,L} → G_L into the group G built from M, determined up to conjugation by Γ = Gal(L/Q). Let Γ_℘ be the decomposition group, L_0 = L^{Γ_℘} and K_0 = L_0 ∩ K. Then L_0 is the smallest field of rationality of v, which is defined as v: G_{m,L_0} → G_{L_0}.

5. Completion. He then passes to the completed local ring at ℘_0 = ℘ ∩ L_0. There are crossed-out attempts mentioning Z_ℓ. He remarks that the data amount to an isomorphism class compatible with transitivity in L, and that an embedding of Z(q^{1/2}) into L is needed. The hypothesis ℘̄ ≠ ℘ appears, tied to imaginary (non-real) Weil numbers.

In modern terms this is the construction of the Weil-number protorus P (the conjectural motivic Galois group of motives over F_q, or its connected part). Its character group is the group of Weil numbers. The cocharacter attached to a choice of prime above p, with field of definition the decomposition field, is the slope/Frobenius cocharacter later used by Langlands–Rapoport, Kottwitz and Milne.
errors: The relation M_0(q) = M_0(p) up to roots of unity is stated loosely. The weight-0 group does not depend on q at all; it is the weight-graded groups M(q) and M(q^n) that are compared through roots of unity and powers.

The text is fragmentary. The precise definition of G and the claim that L_0 is the minimal field of rationality are asserted without proof. The claim is plausible because v_℘ is Γ-equivariant, so its stabiliser is the decomposition group.
The attempt involving Z_ℓ is crossed out; the correct local object at ℘ is p-adic. The line of thought is visibly unfinished.

ideas.what: Group of q-Weil numbers in a CM field, integral away from p, as the character group of the motivic Galois group over F_q
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number protorus P (pseudo-motivic group) for motives over F_q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (oral) and Serre; written up by Langlands–Rapoport (1987) and Milne ('Motives over finite fields', 1994)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's publications. Milne and Serre attribute the idea to Grothendieck in the 1960s.

ideas.what: Weight-0 Weil numbers modulo roots of unity embed into the anti-invariant part of Z^{primes above p} via valuations (Kronecker)
ideas.modern_name: Description of the character group of the weight-0 Weil-number torus by p-adic valuations; slopes

ideas.what: Choice of a prime ℘ above p gives a cocharacter G_m → G defined over the decomposition field L_0 = L^{Γ_℘}
ideas.modern_name: Slope/Frobenius cocharacter ν of the pseudomotivic group (Langlands–Rapoport ν, Kottwitz's Newton map)

missed.claim: This is dated 1965 documentary evidence that Grothendieck explicitly built the Weil-number group for motives over F_q. He also attached to a prime above p a cocharacter whose minimal field of definition is the decomposition field. This anticipates the slope cocharacter of Langlands–Rapoport (1987) and Milne (1994). The general attribution of the Weil-number torus to Grothendieck is known; this specific cocharacter construction is not usually credited to him.
missed.quote: Soit Γ_℘ le groupe de décomposition ... L_0 le corps des invariants de Γ_℘, K_0=L_0∩K. Alors L_0 est le plus petit corps de rationalité de v
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical credit for the pseudomotivic group and its slope cocharacter, which are central to the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture on points of Shimura varieties mod p.

deep.surprise_reason: The Weil-number torus is already informally attributed to Grothendieck. This page gives a concrete early draft, including the decomposition-field cocharacter, but it is fragmentary and adds no new mathematics beyond Langlands–Rapoport and Milne.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring pages (typed English on PSL(2) centralisers and on H^1 of line bundles) are unrelated inserts; only this handwritten sheet belongs to the motif notes.
The margin likely reads 'N.B. M_0(q) = M_0(p) (racines de l'unité près)' and 'α∈L entiers et unités exc. p et satisfait αᾱ=1'.
'On veut construire le groupe de Galois motivique G(q)' (or similar) at the top; 'M_0(q)/Torsion ↪ (Z^P)′'.
Near the end, 'Z(q^{1/2})' is probably meant rather than 'Z(q^2)', i.e. adjoining √q to L.
